intro: The abbreviations and terms below are used throughout this capstone. Currency amounts are in US dollars unless stated otherwise; dollar equivalents of naira, shilling, pound and euro figures are approximate and use the rates given in the cited reports.

terms.definition: Third-party logistics: an outside provider that handles delivery and fulfilment on a company’s behalf
Financing for an identifiable asset or receivable (a loan book, devices, payment float, inventory, vehicles or warehouses), as distinct from platform capital
Africa Private Capital Association (formerly the African Private Equity and Venture Capital Association)
British International Investment, the UK’s development finance institution (formerly CDC Group)
German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung)
Buy-now-pay-later: short-term credit that lets a buyer pay for goods in instalments
CDC Group, former name of British International Investment (BII)
A committed borrowing limit from a lender that a company can draw on. A facility is not a loan book, and the amount drawn may be less than the amount available
Development finance institution: a government-backed lender or investor with a development mandate
Development Partners International, an Africa-focused private equity firm
European Bank for Reconstruction and Development
Dutch Entrepreneurial Development Bank (Nederlandse Financierings-Maatschappij voor Ontwikkelingslanden)
Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit, Germany’s development cooperation agency
Gross merchandise value: the total value of goods sold through a marketplace
International Finance Corporation, the private-sector arm of the World Bank Group
German state-owned development bank (Kreditanstalt für Wiederaufbau)
Know your customer: identity and risk checks on customers
The portfolio of loans or receivables a company has extended to customers and carries on its own balance sheet
Limited partner: an investor in a venture capital or private equity fund
Financing for technology, people, licences, compliance and market entry, which create no separable asset a lender can underwrite
Point of sale (card and payment terminals)
Simple agreement for future equity: a convertible instrument that becomes equity at a later priced round
Pooling loans or receivables in a separate vehicle that issues bonds to investors, repaid from the pooled collections
Stock-keeping unit: a distinct product listed for sale
